title: Idempotent CI pipeline for VPC IaC with policy-driven preflight and safe upgrades
creator: Sophie Alvarez
description: Build an idempotent, auditable Terraform CI pipeline for Redwood Private VPC modules that enforces policy-as-code (OPA/Conftest) during PR plan evaluation, supports automatic drift detection, and provides a safe, reversible apply workflow for tenant upgrades. The pipeline should produce clear remediation suggestions, annotate PRs with plan/policy evidence, and include a self-service recovery path for failed or partial applies to minimize customer downtime.
background: We have recurring incidents and manual toil during Private/VPC upgrades: failed applies, state lock contention, and unclear policy failure signals. Existing pipelines run Conftest/OPA but outputs are noisy and often require engineering intervention. Customers and support teams need deterministic preflight checks that are actionable and a documented recovery runbook for upgrade failures. This ticket implements a new generation of the IaC pipeline that prioritizes idempotency, preflight fidelity, and automated safe rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline integrates with existing monorepo Terraform modules for VPC and networking and runs in PR context producing a human-readable plan artifact (JSON and HTML diff)
OPA/Conftest policy evaluation runs against the plan JSON with structured evidence; failures create annotated comments in PR with links to failing rules and suggested fixes
Pre-apply gates: plan-score threshold, critical OPA failures block merge; optional advisory checks surface but do not block
Idempotent apply step: uses explicit state locking, preflight health checks (API/VPC-level probes), and executes a two-phase apply with canary and finalization stages configurable per-release
Automated drift detector runs post-apply (scheduled) and files PRs for detected resource drift with suggested terraform import/patch recommendations
Operator runbook included: one-click rollback instructions, state recovery steps, and recommended commands for common failure modes
Artifacts: plans, policy-evidence, logs, and state snapshots are archived to S3/GCS for 30 days and surfaced in the PR/build UI
Pipeline idempotency validated by a test harness: repeated plan/apply cycles against a sandbox produce stable state and no duplicate resource creation
Security review completed and IAM least-privilege roles for pipeline service account documented
Documentation: engineering onboarding doc, step-by-step runbook, and a short demo video (3–5 minutes)
tasks: Design pipeline flowchart and failure modes matrix
Prototype plan-as-code adapter that emits Terraform plan JSON and a normalized resource diff
Integrate OPA/Conftest with custom rules for Redwood VPC baseline (encryption, network ACLs, tags, region constraints)
Implement PR annotation bot that posts policy evidence and renders plan HTML
Add plan scoring heuristic and threshold configuration per project
Implement two-phase apply (canary + finalize) with automatic pause and health checks
Build state-locking and recovery helpers that surface conflicts and recommended resolution commands
Implement scheduled drift detection job and PR automation for detected drift
Wire artifact storage and short-term retention for troubleshooting
Author operator runbook and run a drill with on-call and support teams
Create integration tests validating idempotency and policy blocking behavior
Prepare security review package and IAM role definitions
notes: Prefer using 'terraform plan -out=plan.binary' then 'terraform show -json' to generate canonical plan JSON for policy evaluation
Plan scoring should combine resource churn, network change surface area, and presence of risky resource types (e.g., route_table overrides)
Consider light-weight plan diff HTML renderer from existing OSS components to avoid building viewer from scratch
Policy rules must be deterministic and avoid relying on provider-assigned values where possible
Two-phase apply: canary executes against a single tenant subnet allocation; if health probes pass for configurable window (default 5m), finalize applies the rest
Recovery helper should capture state snapshot and export state file before any rollback operation
risks: Complexity of canary semantics across multi-tenant Dedicated pools may require per-tenant config
OPA rules that are too strict could materially increase review time and block legitimate changes
State locking edge cases with long-running applies; need robust lock timeout and stale-lock remediation
S3/GCS artifact retention must meet compliance expectations for Private deployments
implementation_plan: Week 1: design & policy rule authoring; finalize plan JSON schema
Week 2: prototype plan extraction, policy runner integration, and PR annotation mockups
Week 3: implement two-phase apply and state-lock helpers in CI runner
Week 4: add automated drift detector and archival of artifacts
Week 5: integration tests, security review, and operator runbook authoring
Week 6: runbook drill, bug fixes, and docs; prepare release notes for private-2026.04
